review.summary: This PR moves `prepare_linked_requirements_more()` out of the resolver and into individual commands so that `pip install --dry-run` and `pip lock` can skip full wheel downloads. The change is well-scoped, but it removes the `req.prepared = True / needs_more_preparation = False` bookkeeping that the resolver previously did, and never reintroduces it in the call sites — which risks state drift in downstream code that reads those flags. Additionally, the dry-run code path in `install.py` still calls `prepare_linked_requirements_more`, which appears to defeat the stated optimization. The new `set_dist`/`get_dist` cache also bypasses the `metadata_directory` branch unconditionally, which could mask freshly-built metadata.

issues.description: Dry-run still calls prepare_linked_requirements_more, defeating the stated fix
issues.detail: In install.py the new `preparer.prepare_linked_requirements_more(...)` call is placed before the pip self-version check and runs unconditionally — including when `--dry-run` is set. The PR description says dry-run should avoid downloading full wheels, but this call performs exactly that 'more preparation' (full download). The call needs to be gated on `not options.dry_run`, or moved below the dry-run early-return.

issues.description: Resolver no longer marks requirements as prepared, leaving stale state flags
issues.detail: The deleted block set `req.prepared = True` and `req.needs_more_preparation = False` after preparation. The new code in commands calls `prepare_linked_requirements_more` but never updates these flags. Any downstream consumer that checks `req.prepared` or `needs_more_preparation` (e.g., to avoid duplicate work or assert invariants) will now see incorrect values, risking double-preparation or skipped installs.

issues.description: get_dist cache shadows metadata_directory after build
issues.detail: `get_dist` now returns `self._distribution` whenever it is set, short-circuiting the `metadata_directory` branch. If a requirement was first seen via PEP-658 metadata (cached dist) and later fully prepared so that `metadata_directory` is populated from a built sdist/wheel, callers will keep getting the older metadata-only distribution instead of the freshly-built one. Consider clearing `_distribution` in `prepare_linked_requirement` when full prep occurs.

issues.description: direct_url_from_link called with source_dir that may be None during metadata-only fetch
issues.detail: In `prepare.py`, `req.download_info = direct_url_from_link(req.link, req.source_dir)` runs during metadata-only fetching, before the requirement is unpacked. `req.source_dir` is typically unset at this point, and `direct_url_from_link` for VCS/local links uses it to compute commit info / paths. This could produce incorrect or incomplete `download_info` for `pip lock` / `--report` output for non-PyPI links.

issues.description: download command reorders save_linked_requirement after more preparation but loses the prior assumption
issues.detail: Previously `save_linked_requirement` ran before `prepare_linked_requirements_more`; now the order is reversed in download.py and wheel.py. `save_linked_requirement` relies on `req.local_file_path` being the downloaded file. After the move, `prepare_linked_requirements_more` may overwrite or finalize the file location. Verify no requirement ends up saved twice or saved from a stale path, especially when PEP-658 metadata was used.

issues.description: set_dist has no docstring and no type-narrowing for the cache invariant
issues.detail: `set_dist` is a one-liner with no docstring explaining when callers should invoke it versus relying on `metadata_directory`. Given that this method now takes precedence in `get_dist`, a short comment documenting that it is intended for PEP-658 metadata-only flows (and should not be called once the wheel is fully prepared) would prevent future misuse.
